question: The February 2025 Technology Adoption Fund launched by IN‑SPACe has earmarked __________ to support private space start‑ups.
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹500 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Technology Adoption Fund**, launched in **February 2025** by **IN-SPACe**, has been established to promote private space start-ups and innovation within India’s space sector.
 
• The fund has earmarked a total of **₹500 crore** to support private space start-ups. This allocation aims to boost research, development, and deployment of advanced space technologies. *Hence, the correct option is ₹500 crore.*
 
• Private space companies and start-ups are expected to benefit significantly from this fund, allowing them to scale their operations and contribute to India’s space exploration goals.
 
• **IN-SPACe** (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center) is a government body established to enable private participation in India’s space activities. This initiative aligns with India’s broader space policy reforms.
 
• The allocation of **₹500 crore** under the Technology Adoption Fund reflects the growing importance of private players in the space industry and the government’s commitment to fostering innovation. *Hence, the statement regarding the fund allocation is correct.*
 
• This funding is expected to accelerate technological advancements in areas such as satellite development, launch vehicles, and space exploration missions, contributing to India’s global competitiveness in the space sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About IN-SPACe:**

 
 
• **IN-SPACe**, or the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center, was established in **2020** as part of India’s space reforms.
 
• Its primary role is to enable and regulate private sector participation in the Indian space industry, ensuring a competitive and innovative space ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Technology Adoption Fund:**
 
 
• The fund aims to provide financial and technical support to private entities working in the space sector, particularly start-ups with innovative ideas and technology.
 
• It is expected to promote advancements in **satellite technology**, **launch vehicles**, and **space exploration tools**.
 
• The fund also aligns with the vision of making India a global hub for space innovation and technology.
 
 
 
• **Private Participation in Space:**
 
 
• India’s space sector is experiencing a significant shift with the inclusion of private players, contributing to faster innovation and development.
 
• Private companies like **Skyroot Aerospace** and **Agnikul Cosmos** are already making significant strides, supported by IN-SPACe and other initiatives.
 
• **Example:** The successful launch of **Vikram-S**, India’s first privately developed rocket, demonstrates the potential of private start-ups in space exploration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of ₹500 crore Allocation:**

 
 
• The **₹500 crore** funding is one of the largest investments made by the Indian government to boost private space innovation.
 
• This allocation is expected to create a conducive environment for start-ups to experiment with new technologies and contribute to India’s space missions.
 
 
 
• **Global Competitiveness:**
 
 
• India’s space reforms, including initiatives like IN-SPACe and the Technology Adoption Fund, are positioning the country as a leader in the global space industry.
 
• This funding will help bridge the gap between India’s public and private sectors, fostering collaboration and innovation.
